concept.concept_description: An Escher staircase is an infinite strictly ascending chain of ideals I_1 strictly contained in I_2 strictly contained in ... that nevertheless has I_1 as an element of the infinite intersection. Impact: a new invariant for non-Noetherian rings that measures how far a ring is from being Noetherian — the algebraic equivalent of Escher's impossible architecture.

concept.concept_description: Zero-knowledge proofs let you convince someone a statement is true without revealing WHY. Apply this to mathematics: a zero-knowledge proof of a theorem T convinces the verifier that T is provable in PA without revealing any step of the proof. Conjecture: Every theorem provable in Peano Arithmetic has a zero-knowledge proof whose communication complexity is polynomial in the length of the theorem statement (not the proof). This follows from the PCP theorem combined with the fact that PA-proofs can be arithmetized. The zero-knowledge protocol: (1) Prover commits to each proof step using a collision-resistant hash. (2) Verifier randomly challenges one proof step. (3) Prover opens that step and shows it follows from the axioms. Repeating O(k) times gives soundness error 2^{-k}. The proof is zero-knowledge because the verifier only sees one random step per challenge. Test: implement a zero-knowledge proof system for propositional tautologies and prove that a verifier learns nothing beyond the validity of the tautology. Impact: mathematicians can certify results without revealing their methods — a mathematical equivalent of sealed-bid auctions for proof strategies.

# Computational evidence

## Small cases

For alphabet size `q` and book length `n`, direct enumeration predicts `q^n` books.

| `q` | `n` | number of books |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 1 | 2 |
| 2 | 2 | 4 |
| 2 | 3 | 8 |
| 3 | 2 | 9 |
| 4 | 4 | 256 |
| 4 | 16 | 4,294,967,296 |

A specified full book is represented once, so its uniform probability is the reciprocal of the table entry. For the mini-library this is `1 / 4,294,967,296`.

For a library of size `L`, the number of functions from books to books is `L^L`. Small cases show the cardinality gap used by the formal obstruction:

| `L` | catalog tables `L^L` |
|---:|---:|
| 2 | 4 |
| 3 | 27 |
| 4 | 256 |
| 5 | 3,125 |

## OEIS search

The fixed-alphabet counts as book length varies are geometric sequences `q^n`; no specialized OEIS identification is needed for the proof. For `q = 4`, the initial terms are `1, 4, 16, 64, 256, 1024, ...`.

## Counterexample hunt and specification checks

The informal claim that no single volume can encode “the catalog” is too strong if “the catalog” means one particular computable enumeration: the base-`q` decoder is a short description of a bijection between addresses and books. The sound counting statement is instead that no book-valued injective encoding can represent **all possible catalog tables**, because there are `L^L > L` such tables for `L ≥ 2`.

Likewise, an exact numerical probability of a “valid Lean 4 proof” cannot be computed from theorem name and alphabet size alone. It depends on a fixed encoding and a fixed decidable acceptance predicate. The formalization exposes that predicate and proves the exact ratio `accepted_count / q^n`.

No counterexample was found to the finite cardinality formulas. Boundary cases were checked conceptually: when `q^n` is 0 or 1, the strict catalog-table gap fails, which is why the theorem assumes `2 ≤ q^n`.

## De Bruijn comparison

A cyclic de Bruijn sequence of order 16 on four symbols has cyclic length `4^16 = 4,294,967,296`, one starting position for each length-16 word. The formal artifact currently verifies a base-four bijective catalog of exactly that many words; it does not claim to have formalized the cyclic overlap construction.

# Future directions

## Completion status

All Lean declarations delivered for this mission now have complete proof terms: the
remaining mixed-radix bridge lemmas were proved, and an inherited Fibonacci
primitive-divisor draft was corrected to state exactly its computationally verified
range (`13 ≤ n ≤ 10000`) rather than leaving an unproved large-index branch.  The
unrestricted Fibonacci tail remains future work and is not asserted as a theorem.

## What is formalized

`Catalog/Main.lean` models a length-`n` book over a `q`-symbol alphabet as `Fin n → Fin q`. It proves a chained collection of results:

1. the library has exactly `q^n` books;
2. base-`q` addresses give a canonical bijective catalog;
3. the alphabet-4, length-16 mini-library has exactly `4^16 = 4,294,967,296` books and is bijectively cataloged;
4. a fixed complete text has uniform probability exactly `1/q^n`;
5. for any Boolean proof checker, the exact acceptance probability is `accepted_count/q^n`, and an accepted witness makes that count positive;
6. there are `(q^n)^(q^n)` catalog tables, so, when at least two books exist, no book-valued injective encoding can represent every possible table;
7. distributed storage of `total` distinct objects in `N` books with `capacity` slots each is possible exactly when `total ≤ N * capacity`.

The single-book impossibility theorem deliberately concerns encoding **every possible catalog table**. It does not incorrectly claim that one particular canonical catalog cannot have a short algorithmic description—the preceding base-`q` catalog is such a description.

## Important qualifications

The exact probability that a string is accepted by “Lean 4” is not a well-defined number until the byte/alphabet encoding, target theorem, permitted imports/environment, parser behavior, resource policy, and checker version are fixed. The formal result therefore parameterizes a finite Boolean checker and gives the exact formula. Supplying an executable model of a particular Lean environment would turn this formula into a concrete finite count, although brute-force evaluation at Babel scale is infeasible.

The requested de Bruijn construction is not yet formalized. The current mini-catalog is a base-four bijective enumeration of all length-16 words, not a cyclic de Bruijn word. A true order-16 de Bruijn cycle over four symbols would have cyclic length `4^16`; proving it should proceed by defining the order-15 de Bruijn directed graph, proving balanced indegree/outdegree and connectivity, obtaining an Eulerian circuit, and proving the resulting cyclic windows occur exactly once.

## Next formal developments

1. Define cyclic words and cyclic length-`n` windows.
2. Formalize the de Bruijn digraph on `Library q (n-1)` and its shift edges.
3. Prove existence of an Eulerian circuit for nonempty finite alphabets.
4. Extract and verify a de Bruijn cycle, then specialize it to alphabet size 4 and order 16.
5. Define a concrete finite tokenization and bounded Lean-like checker, allowing executable small-case acceptance counts.
6. Refine distributed storage from abstract slots to bit capacity, with explicit ceiling bounds and prefix-free/self-delimiting encodings.
7. Study substring occurrence probabilities. For a fixed pattern, the naive `(n-k+1)q^{-k}` is a union bound rather than generally an equality because overlapping occurrences are dependent; exact counts can be obtained with finite automata or inclusion–exclusion.

lemma prime_eq_three_of_three_dvd {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (h3 : 3 ∣ p) : p = 3 := by
  rw [ hp.dvd_iff_eq ] at h3 <;> aesop

lemma prime_mod_nine_ne_zero {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : p % 9 ≠ 0 := by
  exact fun h => by have := Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero h; rw [ hp.dvd_iff_eq ] at this <;> norm_num [ this ] at *;

/-- A prime cannot be congruent to six modulo nine. -/
lemma prime_mod_nine_ne_six {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : p % 9 ≠ 6 := by
  exact fun had ↦ absurd ( Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero ( show p % 3 = 0 from by omega ) ) ( by rw [ hp.dvd_iff_eq ] <;> omega )

has two prime fangs, only three of the six unrestricted residue pairs survive. -/

    (h : VampireWitness v x y) (hx : x.Prime) (hy : y.Prime) :
    (x % 9, y % 9) = (2, 2) ∨
    (x % 9, y % 9) = (5, 8) ∨
    (x % 9, y % 9) = (8, 5) := by
  rcases vampire_fangs_residue_sieve h with h | h | h | h | h | h <;> simp_all +decide;
  · have := Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero h.1; have := Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero h.2; simp_all +decide [ Nat.Prime.dvd_iff_eq ] ;

vampire witness and two prime fangs is congruent to four modulo nine. -/
theorem prime_fang_product_mod_nine {v x y : ℕ}
    (h : VampireWitness v x y) (hx : x.Prime) (hy : y.Prime) :
    v % 9 = 4 := by
  rcases h with ⟨ rfl, h ⟩;
  have := prime_fang_residue_sieve ⟨ rfl, h ⟩ hx hy; rcases this with ( h | h | h ) <;> simp_all +decide [ Nat.mul_mod ] ;

    ¬ 3 ∣ v := by
  exact fun h' => by have := prime_fang_product_mod_nine h hx hy; omega;

    (h : VampireWitness v x y) (hx : x.Prime) (hy : y.Prime) :

    (x % 9, y % 9) = (5, 8) ∨

vampire witness and two prime fangs is congruent to four modulo nine. -/

    (h : VampireWitness v x y) (hx : x.Prime) (hy : y.Prime) :

The existing exact digit witnesses establish the following first seven decimal vampire factorizations:

|---:|---:|---:|
| 1260 | 21 × 60 | (3, 6) |
| 1395 | 15 × 93 | (6, 3) |

Every pair belongs to the six-point unrestricted residue sieve
`(0,0), (2,2), (3,6), (5,8), (6,3), (8,5)`. None of these seven examples has two prime fangs.

The classical smallest witness is exact at the digit-multiset level:
`digits(21) + digits(60)` is a permutation of `digits(1260)`.

The proposed “zombie” description is inconsistent: it says both fangs are prime, but the supplied factorizations of `125460` use `204 × 615` and `246 × 510`, in each case two composite factors. The prime-fang interpretation was retained because it is the literal definition and leads to a falsifiable arithmetic class.

The claim that density “approaches `1/√n`” should be read as an asymptotic scale, since `1/√n` itself approaches zero. A precise conjecture needs a counting function, denominator, and leading constant.

No exhaustive enumeration up to `10^8` is reported here. Such a table would depend sensitively on resolving the ambiguous werewolf and zombie definitions, and an unchecked external computation would not support the universal theorems proved in this cycle.

## OEIS search

No OEIS identifier is asserted. The standard vampire-number sequence is widely tabulated, but no external sequence lookup was performed during this cycle, so assigning an identifier would risk an unsupported citation.

## Structural table for prime fangs

Intersecting the exact unrestricted residue sieve with primality leaves:

| `x mod 9` | `y mod 9` | `(x·y) mod 9` |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 2 | 4 |
| 5 | 8 | 4 |
| 8 | 5 | 4 |

Thus every decimal digit-permutation product with two prime fangs lies in the single residue class `4 mod 9`. This table is proved for all natural-number witnesses in `Catalog/Algebra/VampirePrimeFangSieve.lean`; it is not merely a bounded search observation.

# Future Directions: Arithmetic Monsters

## 1. Square-root density with a precise normalization

Let `V(n)` be the proportion of `2n`-digit decimal integers that admit a classical vampire factorization with two `n`-digit fangs. Determine whether `√n · V(n)` converges to a positive finite constant, and identify that constant if it exists. This formulation separates the claimed `1/√n` scale from an unspecified leading factor and makes the claim falsifiable.

**The key insight is...** digit permutations impose both a multinomial occupancy constraint and the modular unit-curve constraint `(x-1)(y-1) ≡ 1 (mod 9)`; a credible density model must combine these rather than count digit permutations alone.

**Why now?** The exact residue sieve supplies a local factor that can be incorporated into a probabilistic count, while the remaining discrepancy can be tested by stratifying candidates by digit-frequency profile.

## 2. Vampire existence in every even-length decade

For every integer `k ≥ 1`, prove or disprove that the interval `[10^(2k), 10^(2k+2))` contains a classical vampire number. A stronger version asks for a family constructed uniformly from `k`, rather than isolated witnesses.

**The key insight is...** length conservation forces a valid fang product into the upper multiplication-length regime, so a construction should control leading digits and the full digit multiset simultaneously.

**Why now?** The known length and residue obstructions sharply specify what any recursive construction must preserve and offer immediate rejection tests for proposed families.

## 3. Infinitude of prime-fang digit-permutation products

Determine whether infinitely many decimal digit-permutation factorizations have both fangs prime. Any such product must have fang residues `(2,2)`, `(5,8)`, or `(8,5)` modulo nine and must itself be congruent to four modulo nine.

**The key insight is...** the combinatorial digit condition cuts out a finite modular curve, and primality collapses that curve to only three admissible points; the problem therefore resembles finding primes in a highly constrained digital family.

**Why now?** The prime-fang concentration law gives the first exact local obstruction and can guide targeted searches or a sieve that distinguishes genuine scarcity from a finite-data artifact.

## 4. Vanishing density of ghost factorizations

Fix a balanced definition in which `x` and `y` have `n` decimal digits and their `2n`-digit product shares no digit value with either factor. Prove that the proportion of such factor pairs tends to zero, preferably with an exponential upper bound.

**The key insight is...** avoidance is governed by the set of digit values present, not merely by digit sums; once either factor exhibits many distinct digits, the product is forced into a rapidly shrinking alphabet.

**Why now?** A balanced model removes trivial size effects and makes entropy, occupancy estimates, and multiplication carries available in one sharply stated problem.

**Why now?** The general casting-out-`(b-1)` law and the complete decimal residue classification provide both the theoretical template and a concrete benchmark for comparisons across bases.

concept.title: ArXiv paper: The chromatic number of 3-stable Kneser graphs
concept.concept_description: Investigate the ArXiv paper 'The chromatic number of 3-stable Kneser graphs' and formalize its key results. Abstract: For an integer $s \ge 2$, a subset $S \subseteq [n]$ is {\em $s$-stable} if $\min \{j - i, n + i - j\}\ge s$ for every $i,j \in S$ with $i<j$. Denote the set of all $s$-stable subsets of size $k$ of $[n]$ by $\binom{[n]}{k}_{s\text{-stable}}$. Schrijver proved in 1978 that whenever $n\ge 2k$, the chromatic number of the Kneser graph $\mathrm{KG}\big( \binom{[n]}{k}_{2\text{-stable}}\big)$ is $n - 2k +2$. Generalizing this result, Meunier conjectured in 2011 that $χ\left( \mathrm{KG}\big( \binom{[n]}{k}_{s\text{-stable}} \big) \right)= n - sk +s$ for all $n\ge sk$. This conjecture was previously proven for all even $s$, for $s \ge 4$ and large enough $n$, and for $k=2$. We prove the conjecture in the cases $s=3$ and $n$ large enough, or $k=s=3$. To this end, we prove versions of the Hilton-Milner theorem for $s$-stable sets. We also present a topological approach towards Meunier's conjecture.

Define a phantom topology on a set X as a function T: O -> Top(X) that assigns to each observer o a topology T(o) on X. open Phantom

variable {X : Type*} {k : ℕ}

/-- The topology agreed upon by a finite coalition of observers. -/
def coalitionJoin (T : Fin k → TopologicalSpace X) (S : Finset (Fin k)) :
    TopologicalSpace X :=
  ⨆ i ∈ S, T i

/-
Coalition joins respect union: combining two coalitions joins their two compressed
views.
-/
theorem coalitionJoin_union (T : Fin k → TopologicalSpace X)
    (S A : Finset (Fin k)) :
    coalitionJoin T (S ∪ A) = coalitionJoin T S ⊔ coalitionJoin T A := by
  refine' le_antisymm _ _ <;> simp +decide [ coalitionJoin ];
  · rintro i ( hi | hi ) <;> [ exact le_sup_of_le_left ( le_iSup₂_of_le i hi le_rfl ) ; exact le_sup_of_le_right ( le_iSup₂_of_le i hi le_rfl ) ];
  · exact ⟨ fun i hi => le_iSup₂_of_le i ( Or.inl hi ) le_rfl, fun i hi => le_iSup₂_of_le i ( Or.inr hi ) le_rfl ⟩

/-
Every cut of the observer set preserves reality: compressing the observers on each
side of `S | Sᶜ` and then taking their consensus gives the original consensus.
-/
theorem consensus_eq_cut (T : Fin k → TopologicalSpace X) (S : Finset (Fin k)) :
    consensus T = coalitionJoin T S ⊔ coalitionJoin T Sᶜ := by
  rw [ ← coalitionJoin_union ];
  unfold coalitionJoin; aesop;

/-- A finite phantom system is coalition-essential over `τ` when every proper coalition
has a join strictly finer than `τ`.  This records the full combinatorial dependency
pattern, rather than merely requiring each individual observer to be strict. -/
def CoalitionEssential (τ : TopologicalSpace X) (T : Fin k → TopologicalSpace X) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset (Fin k), S ⊂ Finset.univ → coalitionJoin T S < τ

/-
**Main cut theorem.** If consensus is `τ` and every proper coalition is strict, then
any nonempty proper cut compresses the system to two strictly finer coalition observers
whose consensus is exactly `τ`.
-/
theorem essential_cut_genuine (τ : TopologicalSpace X) (T : Fin k → TopologicalSpace X)
    (hcons : consensus T = τ) (hessential : CoalitionEssential τ T)
    (S : Finset (Fin k)) (hne : S.Nonempty) (hproper : S ≠ Finset.univ) :
    coalitionJoin T S < τ ∧ coalitionJoin T Sᶜ < τ ∧
      coalitionJoin T S ⊔ coalitionJoin T Sᶜ = τ := by
  refine' ⟨ hessential S _, hessential Sᶜ _, _ ⟩;
  · exact lt_of_le_of_ne ( Finset.subset_univ _ ) hproper;
  · simp +decide [ Finset.ssubset_def, Finset.subset_iff ];
    exact hne;
  · rw [ ← consensus_eq_cut, hcons ]

Any genuine finite representation with at least two observers has a genuine binary
compression.  This connects the coalition cut calculus to the general complete-lattice
collapse theorem established in the phantom-topology theory.
-/
theorem finite_family_has_binary_compression (τ : TopologicalSpace X)
    (T : Fin k → TopologicalSpace X) (hk : 2 ≤ k)
    (hcons : consensus T = τ) (hstrict : ∀ i, T i < τ) :
    ∃ B : Fin 2 → TopologicalSpace X,
      consensus B = τ ∧ ∀ i, B i < τ := by
  apply Phantom.finite_collapses_to_two τ T hk hcons hstrict

On the Euclidean real line, the established lower- and upper-limit observers form a
binary compression in which both observers are strictly finer than reality.
-/
theorem real_line_binary_witness :
    ∃ B : Fin 2 → TopologicalSpace ℝ,

        ∀ i, B i < (inferInstance : TopologicalSpace ℝ) := by
  exact ⟨Phantom.euclideanObservers, Phantom.euclidean_has_genuine_two_rep⟩

# Future Directions: Coalition Geometry of Phantom Topologies

## 1. Circuit classification of minimal observer systems

**Conjecture.** For every finite carrier, coalition-minimal phantom representations are precisely the circuits of the join-dependency closure on the lattice of topologies. Equivalently, a finite observer family is coalition-essential exactly when its index set is a minimal dependent set for the equation equating its join with reality.

The key insight is that the cut theorem replaces observer counting by a Boolean pattern of proper coalitions: every proper coalition retains excess resolution, while the whole family loses it. This is the signature of a circuit rather than an ordinary generating set.

**Why now?** Coalition joins and their behavior under cuts are explicit, and finite topology lattices provide a concrete testbed in which circuits can be enumerated and compared with standard dependency axioms.

## 2. A forbidden-minor theory for phantom rigidity

**Conjecture.** Join-irreducible finite topologies admit a finite forbidden-minor characterization under two operations: restriction to a subset and quotient by a topological indistinguishability relation.

The key insight is that phantom rigidity is join-irreducibility, while restriction and quotient are the natural topology-level analogues of deletion and contraction. A successful minor theory would convert a lattice obstruction into a structural classification of spaces.

**Why now?** Rigidity is already visible on the two-point Sierpiński space, and the coalition viewpoint identifies the exact property that must survive or fail under minor operations.

## 3. Algebraic dependence controls Zariski observer circuits

**Conjecture.** For affine algebraic sets, minimal genuine observer families obtained by selectively resolving zero loci correspond to circuits in the algebraic matroid of the coordinate ring.

The key insight is that a Zariski topology is generated by polynomial equations, while coalition-essentiality records when no proper subfamily of observers recovers all common opens. Minimal algebraic dependencies are therefore natural candidates for minimal consensus dependencies.

**Why now?** The cofinite affine line already has an explicit two-observer split, so the next falsifiable step is to test whether higher-dimensional Zariski examples organize their phantom decompositions according to algebraic matroid circuits.

## 4. Infinite consensus and compactness failure

**Conjecture.** There exists a topology that is the consensus of an infinite family of strict observers but is not the consensus of any finite family of strict observers; moreover, the least such cardinal is controlled by a join-compactness invariant of the topology lattice.

The key insight is that every finite genuine representation collapses to two, so any genuinely new numerical hierarchy must occur at infinite cardinalities. The obstruction should be failure of compactness for joins below the target topology.

**Why now?** The finite theory is complete enough to isolate the only remaining regime. This makes an infinite example sharply testable: every finite subfamily must retain strictly more resolution than the full consensus.

## 5. Complexity of detecting phantom rigidity on finite spaces

**Conjecture.** When a finite topology is supplied by its minimal basis, deciding whether it is phantom-rigid is coNP-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, while non-rigidity always has a polynomial-size certificate consisting of two strict refinements whose consensus is the input topology.

**Why now?** The binary collapse theorem fixes the certificate shape at two observers, eliminating an unbounded search over family sizes. The minimal-basis input model and two-refinement certificate now make both membership in coNP and a hardness reduction concrete, separately testable targets.
